answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake to transact, and let trust grow from verified useful work randomly sampled. A new identity starts in a shallow lagoon of low limits: small jobs only, its cap rising after peer-checked completions. Fakes gain nothing from numbers, because each identity must separately fund a stake and build history; splitting funds yields weak copies, not one powerful account. Fraud forfeits the stake, like an opal losing its fire, while honest agents keep an ivory-clean record, so each sybil face costs money and time with no shortcut to trust.
